body:
WHAT
Settings are read from three layers: schema defaults, the global file `~/.magentra/settings.json`, then the project file `<cwd>/.magentra/settings.json`; each later layer deep-merges over the earlier one and selected env vars override everything. `/settings` prints each leaf key with its effective value and the layer it came from (default, global, project or env).

WHY
Without layering a per-project model or endpoint would have to be re-typed globally; without source attribution a user cannot see why a value differs from what they set.

WHERE
engine/core/src/config/settings.ts — loadSettings(cwd) (global then project via deepMerge, then applyEnvOverrides), globalSettingsPath(), projectSettingsPath(), deepMerge(), ENV_OVERRIDES, describeSettings(cwd) (source attribution via flattenLeaves), SettingSourceKind. Rendered by engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — Engine.renderSettings().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With global {model:'g'} and project {model:'p'}, loadSettings(cwd).settings.model === 'p' and describeSettings(cwd) reports key 'model' with source 'project'.
2. With only global {search:{provider:'brave'}} and project {search:{enabled:false}}, the effective search is {enabled:false, provider:'brave'} (nested deep merge), with search.enabled sourced 'project' and search.provider sourced 'global'.
3. A key set in neither file (e.g. compactionThreshold) is reported with source 'default' and the schema default value.
4. With process.env.MAGENTRA_MODEL='e' and model set in both files, the effective model is 'e' and its source is 'env'; a blank env var ('') does not override.
5. An unknown key in a file produces a warning entry, not a throw, and invalid JSON in one layer yields a warning while the other layer still loads.
